findings: The REJECT verdict is a FALSE NEGATIVE from stale source, not a valid rejection. The worker read the Owner's LOCAL checkout (C:/Users/Rudy2/project-keystone + C:/Users/Rudy2/Taylor_Parts), which is behind origin/main, and reviewed the pre-cockpit v1.1 board — schema 1.1.0, no cockpitSection, no projectCockpit — none of which is the merged deliverable (#15 / #744 / #745).

Orchestration finding (real, distinct from the wake FUTURE_SEAM): dispatched review agents read the Owner's LOCAL filesystem, which drifts behind merged main. A 'route a review' can therefore produce a verdict against stale code unless the review target is a fresh checkout. Mitigation used: re-route (ACCEPT-002) against fresh origin/main worktrees.
One genuinely useful signal survived the contamination and was independently confirmed against the real code by ACCEPT-002: the pre-fix app.js blank-on-refresh-failure (already fixed in #14).

evidence.note: read-only; reviewed STALE local checkout; verdict invalidated by source freshness

questionsRaised: Should the Owner update their LOCAL project-keystone + Taylor_Parts checkouts (git pull on main) before any local-source review or hosted publish? (An Owner action — the launcher detects+reports stale, never auto-pulls.)
scenariosDiscovered: Review-agent source freshness is a first-class orchestration concern: a review request should target a known-fresh checkout, or record the reviewed commit so a stale review is detectable and disposable.
contaminationReason: read the Owner's local checkout (behind origin/main); reviewed the pre-cockpit v1.1 board, not the merged cockpit
